operations.evidence: crime, anti-social behaviour and outcome data are published on a monthly frequency
monthly publication is not a real-time incident feed
the published dataset covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland
coverage and contributing organisations differ by data type and jurisdiction
the dataset is made available under the Open Government Licence v3.0
the licence does not remove privacy, attribution or source-quality constraints
complete monthly CSV archives use a consistent year-month URL structure
archive availability does not imply that every force-month is complete or revision-free
custom CSV download and JSON API interfaces are provided for accessing subsets instead of the full archive
subset queries can omit records outside the requested time or geometry
the Reported by field identifies the force that supplied the crime data
the supplying force is not necessarily a parcel-level jurisdictional determination
the Falls within field currently also identifies the supplying force and is under review
the field must not be treated as a stable independent geographic classification
published LSOA fields refer to the LSOA containing the anonymised map point
the LSOA may reflect the anonymised point rather than the exact incident location
Last outcome category refers to the most recent outcome associated with the crime
the field is not a complete case history and can change after later updates
data are supplied by geographic police forces, British Transport Police, Police Service of Northern Ireland and the Ministry of Justice
provider coverage varies by record type and should be retained during joins
each force generates monthly Crime and ASB and Police Outcomes files in a prescribed format
file generation processes vary across force source systems
crime records sent to the Ministry of Justice are matched to available court results and returned for integration
court-result matching is not guaranteed to find every relevant record
siloed force systems can require manual joining and double-keying, increasing quality risk
the caveat does not quantify error for an individual force-month
the monthly Crime and ASB file contains records for incidents from the previous month
published records are transformed and anonymised before release
a monthly outcomes file can contain updates for crimes that occurred many months earlier
outcome month must not be assumed to equal crime month
uploaded outcomes are joined to original crimes using the offence reference before publication
the raw offence reference is not published and unmatched outcomes can remain
the raw offence reference is replaced by a one-way hash published as persistent_id
persistent_id is a publication identifier and not a parcel identifier
crime and outcome dates are truncated to year and month before publication
day-level incident or outcome timing cannot be inferred
Home Office offence codes are mapped into published crime categories
the broad category does not preserve every source offence-code distinction
published latitude and longitude represent approximate anonymised locations rather than exact incident coordinates
coordinates must not be used as exact parcel evidence
anonymous map points are selected to contain at least eight postal addresses or no postal addresses
a snap point can aggregate multiple possible premises
exact crime coordinates are replaced by the nearest approved map point and are zeroed if that point is more than 20 kilometres away
distance displacement and zero coordinates require fail-closed spatial handling
force geocoding practices are inconsistent and published location accuracy is not fully consistent
location fields cannot independently support a high-confidence parcel match
uploads are rejected when required formatting, valid-date, required-field or geographic checks fail
passing format validation does not prove semantic correctness
forces review upload summaries and approve data as suitable for publication
provider approval is a quality control rather than independent remeasurement
manual review checks monthly changes, missing locations, failed anonymisation, boundary anomalies, free text and outcome joins
manual review can reduce but not eliminate data-quality issues
street-level crime can be queried within a one-mile radius or a custom polygon
query geometry is a retrieval boundary and not proof that an incident occurred at a parcel
custom areas containing more than 10,000 crimes return an HTTP 503 response
large-area failures must not be interpreted as zero crime
latitude and longitude crime-at-location queries resolve to the nearest predefined location
the returned location is not an exact coordinate match
street-level outcomes are not available for the Police Service of Northern Ireland
absence of outcome rows for Northern Ireland is a coverage limitation rather than a zero outcome count
open files provide record-level collision, vehicle and casualty data from 1979
the files describe reported road collisions and do not establish parcel safety
